section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of Sine Powers
section_1.content: Introduce the integral of sin^n(x) from 0 to π/2. Explain the reduction formula (Wallis Integrals) visually as the area under a curve that 'flattens' as n increases.
section_1.example: Visualize the area shrinking: compare sin^1(x) (quarter-circle curve) to sin^10(x) (a thin spike hugging the y-axis).

section_2.title: Deriving the Ratio: The Key Insight
section_2.content: Show the ratio of two consecutive Wallis integrals, I_{2n+1} / I_{2n}. Explain that as n approaches infinity, this ratio approaches 1. This is the foundation for isolating π.
section_2.example: An animated 'tug-of-war' between two shrinking shapes where the gap between them eventually vanishes.

section_3.title: The Wallis Product Formula
section_3.content: Reveal the infinite product formula: π/2 = (2/1 * 2/3) * (4/3 * 4/5) * (6/5 * 6/7) .... Connect the algebraic terms to the limiting process derived in the previous section.
section_3.example: A mechanical assembly line where a robot (let's name him 'Wallis-Bot') repeatedly multiplies fractions, with the output value slowly converging to 1.5707... on a digital display.

section_4.title: Intuition: Why Pi?
section_4.content: Discuss why this infinite product involves only integers. Explain the 'beauty' of infinite series/products—taking discrete rational numbers and arriving at the transcendental constant π.
section_4.example: A 'Pixel-Cat' character trying to measure a circular yarn ball; each fraction in the product represents one step of the cat tracing the circumference.

section_5.title: Summary & Real-World Significance
section_5.content: Recap: Wallis Integrals -> Ratio -> Infinite Product. Mention how such approximations were historically vital for calculation before modern supercomputers.
section_5.example: A closing animation showing the number 'π' being built like a scaffold, layer by layer, out of infinitely many floating numerical fractions.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])
